chapter: Singers, Las Vegas, Hodges and road life
title: Turk Van Lake and the Peck Kelly story
summary: Guitarist Turk Van Lake would not leave New York, which Barnet compares to Houston pianist Peck Kelly.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah. You had Turk Van Lake.

Oh, Turk? A guitar player. When Turk was working with me he hadn't gotten in much, into arranging. He was just strictly, you know, a guitarist. And he wasn't with me too long because Turk didn't want to leave New York. He -- like the old story about Peck Kelly, did you ever hear of him?

Well, he was a fabulous piano player that lived back in the '20s, and he lived in Houston, Texas, and people would come from all over the country. He was just a fabulous piano player. And the old story was yeah, but you can't get him to leave town. He had offers from Paul Whiteman, no, he wouldn't leave. He stayed. I had the good fortune of

hearing him play. It was just fantastic. Of course the old school of piano, the full stride, Art Tatum type things, and in other words, the piano player in that school of piano, they had to sound like a whole band. They played their own accompaniment and the band and the solos and everything, but he was absolutely fabulous, but he would not leave Houston, Texas. And that's Turk Van Lake. I mean he would not leave New York.
